title: QUIET VESSEL
territory: A broad held thought, open above: expression gathers in a substantial body and leaves through one deliberate asymmetry.
oneSentenceMeaning: Mluva gives a spoken thought somewhere steady to take shape, while keeping its opening to the world clear.
appIdentity: Mluva is a calm, immediate companion for turning speech into text that still belongs to the speaker. Its Czech name means speech or manner of speaking, which gives the identity a human starting point without requiring a mascot. On Omarchy, delight comes from a small tool fitting everyday work: speak, see a draft, refine it, and return to the task. The product keeps original recognition, edited source, and completed rewrites distinct; editable Markdown makes that care tangible. Its open-source character suggests an intelligible, approachable instrument. Local and cloud providers are choices, so the identity must not imply that every operation stays on the device. Quiet Vessel expresses the pleasure of having enough room for a thought and enough structure to retain it. It supports Most delightful dictation for Omarchy and A little more delight every day through composed confidence rather than a promise of flawless recognition.
markIdentity: Quiet Vessel treats speaking as something that can gather before it becomes a finished sentence. One substantial filled body carries a broad opening at its upper edge. The opening is displaced, and its shoulders do not match: one holds, while the other makes room for expression to continue. This controlled imbalance gives a still mark a sense of readiness. The mass should feel generous and compact, with enough ink to survive a panel or launcher at 24 pixels. The vessel is a spatial idea rather than an illustrated object. It has no handle, rim ellipse, feet, face, speech tail, microphone capsule, droplets, or sound bars. A single memorable negative-space cut must do the expressive work. The intended emotional reading is that a thought is welcome here and will remain available for further shaping. That interpretation fits source retention and rewriting, but it makes no claim about provider privacy, guaranteed accuracy, or autonomous action.
logoDescription:
The initial study begins with a low, generous body of ink, approximately five units wide for every four units high. Its outside contour is continuous and softly compressed, with broad sides flowing into a full lower belly. The upper edge is interrupted by one large open chamber. Viewed quickly, the mass feels as if it is holding something that has not yet become visible. There are no separate particles or interior marks to stand in for words. The chamber is the thought's available space, and the surrounding body gives that space a calm presence.

Place the chamber slightly to the right of the geometric center. Its left boundary descends from a tall, broad shoulder; its right boundary returns to a shoulder that sits visibly lower. The chamber's floor is initially a restrained curve, flatter than the exterior belly. The difference between the inner and outer contours is essential: this must be a heavy, filled form with a carved opening, never a line drawing of a container. The base should carry nearly half the symbol's height, making the body look occupied and dependable rather than hollow.

Let the lower right shoulder turn outward only slightly, producing a quiet speaking opening without a pointed speech tail. That change in direction is the sole expressive event. Keep every other transition slow and resolved. The left side supplies stability, the lowered right side supplies permission to continue, and the broad lower mass supplies visual memory. Do not add a second notch to force an M, or a floating accent to imply voice. The symbol should belong to Mluva through its proportions and opening, not through a rebus.

Render the study as one flat, opaque ink shape on actual transparency. The first test is a clean silhouette at 24 pixels, followed by light and dark reversals. At that scale, the chamber must remain visibly open and the shoulder difference must survive without relying on antialiasing. Larger presentations should reveal careful contour tension, not extra detail. In the film, this quiet weight can sit comfortably near water and the breathing surface, while retaining an identity that works alone on a static desktop.
wordmarkDescription:
The initial wordmark spells Mluva exactly, with an uppercase M and lowercase luva. Start from JetBrains Mono Medium outlines to retain the product's existing relationship with its interface, then redraw the five letters as a single considered piece of lettering. Preserve the font's upright stance, useful distinctions, and plainspoken rhythm. Allow optical widths and spacing to depart from fixed cells: the l should occupy less horizontal space, while the M should feel broad enough to begin the word with assurance. The result should read immediately as a name before any custom geometry is noticed.

Use the u as the first place to explore the vessel idea. Broaden its lower bowl slightly and flatten the deepest part of its inner space, retaining clear vertical stems and an unmistakable u. Keep the right terminal modestly lower than the left, using a visible but restrained asymmetry. This treatment should suggest the same held space as the symbol without inserting the symbol itself into the word. The lowercase a keeps a recognizable double-storey structure; enlarge its lower counter and soften the counter's lower corners so it belongs to the same family of spaces.

The M retains its two upright outer stems and clear internal valley. Open that valley enough to avoid a dark knot at display sizes. Narrow the l while preserving its recognizable terminal treatment, then adjust the Ml and lu pairs optically so the word does not appear to split after the capital. Keep the v crisp, with slight optical softening only where its diagonals meet. Its sharp internal space gives useful articulation between the rounded u and a.

Choose substantial ink, closer in visual weight to a carefully drawn medium than a delicate monospaced specimen. Customization should be concentrated in bowl shape, counter area, and terminal balance. No ligatures, cut-through gimmicks, missing stems, accent marks, detached pieces, or stretched letterforms. Deliver only the five-letter wordmark on real transparency, without a symbol, descriptor, tagline, baseline, or framing device.

selfCritique.risk: The vessel story may merely rationalize an ordinary bowl.
selfCritique.adversarialReading: A soft belly and a curved inner floor form a familiar smiling container. Unequal shoulders alone may look like imprecise drawing rather than authorship.
selfCritique.response: Replace the curved chamber floor with a broad, nearly level ledge and a single short rising transition. Flatten the outside base and enlarge the difference in shoulder height. The final silhouette must be recognized by these structural decisions.

selfCritique.risk: The speaking shoulder may become a bird beak or speech-bubble tail.
selfCritique.adversarialReading: Any outward flick offers an easy image-generation shortcut, but it changes the category from held thought to an animal or chat icon.
selfCritique.response: Remove the outward flick entirely. Keep the right shoulder within the original hull and use only its lower height and inward-facing terminal to imply release.

selfCritique.risk: Too much hollow space makes the design an outline in disguise.
selfCritique.adversarialReading: A thick U is still a rim, and its long uniform band may resemble an unrelated utility icon or a smiling mouth.
selfCritique.response: Make the lower mass substantially thicker than either shoulder. Keep the opening shallow enough to read as a carved recess in a filled body, with no constant-width band.

selfCritique.risk: The broad body could become an app tile or an arbitrary rounded block.
selfCritique.adversarialReading: A rounded rectangle with a notch may be compact but emotionally blank, and the upper recess might look like a folder or crown.
selfCritique.response: Retain gently convex side flanks, broad lower corner transitions, and only a short flattened base. Avoid four equal corner radii, a full rectangular perimeter, and repeated upper teeth.

selfCritique.risk: The lowered u terminal could read as a damaged letter.
selfCritique.adversarialReading: At modest wordmark sizes, a one-pixel height difference is more likely to suggest rasterization failure than a vessel reference.
selfCritique.response: Restore a shared lowercase terminal height. Move the distinctive treatment into the u's inner bowl and the a's counter, where it remains legible without broken alignment.

selfCritique.risk: The lettering may still be ordinary JetBrains Mono with altered tracking.
selfCritique.adversarialReading: Narrowing l and opening counters repeats existing brand work; it does not establish a strong alternative wordmark.
selfCritique.response: Give the u a clearly wider internal ledge, redraw the a's lower counter with related geometry, and broaden the M's central negative valley while keeping every letter conventional enough to read.

selfCritique.risk: The metaphor could overpromise privacy or retention.
selfCritique.adversarialReading: A safe vessel can suggest that nothing leaves the device or that all captured content is permanently protected, neither of which describes every provider and mode.
selfCritique.response: Describe steadiness, source continuity, and room to edit. Exclude shields, locks, local-only claims, and language implying that the symbol certifies a security property.

revision.decision: Keep the held-space territory. Replace the soft bowl construction with a denser body and a deliberately sculpted upper recess. The following final descriptions supersede the initial descriptions and govern both generation prompts.
revision.finalLogoDescription:
The final mark is a compact, solid body with one broad recess carved downward from its upper edge. Its proportion is approximately 100 wide by 80 high. The left shoulder is taller and broader; the right shoulder begins about 14 units lower and stays fully inside the outer hull. The recess occupies roughly 42 percent of the width, centered slightly right of the body's midpoint. It reaches only about 36 units below the highest shoulder. This leaves a substantial lower mass, making the mark feel full rather than like a hollow rim.

The upper recess has two quiet sides and a distinct floor. Its left wall descends almost vertically before turning through a generous internal corner into a short, nearly level ledge. That ledge transitions upward toward the lower right shoulder through one broad, softened diagonal. The diagonal is internal; nothing projects from the perimeter. The opening remains entirely connected to the transparent space above. There are no enclosed holes, separate objects, secondary slits, or ornamental lines. This single asymmetrical recess is the mark's identifying feature.

Outside, retain a calm convex left flank and a slightly tighter right flank. Both turn into generous lower corners, joined by a short flattened base occupying about one third of the width. The base is subtly left of geometric center to balance the higher shoulder. Avoid a full semicircle and avoid a rounded rectangle. The silhouette should feel shaped and weighty, with unequal distributions of ink that make its held-space idea visible even before explanation. At small sizes, the upper opening, shoulder difference, and dense base must all remain obvious.

No lip, pointed spout, outward flick, face, handle, pedestal, droplet, flower petal, microphone, or speech tail survives the revision. The result is an abstract app symbol with a specific topography, not an illustration of a physical vessel. One monochrome fill supplies its entire identity. Recognition should come from the mass and the asymmetric opening, with warmth supplied by the corner transitions. Its affinity with water and breathing is a matter of composure and slight motion, never liquid texture or a changing blob.
revision.finalWordmarkDescription:
The final lettering remains exactly Mluva, with a capital M, a narrow lowercase l, and clearly separated u, v, and double-storey a. JetBrains Mono Medium supplies the initial skeleton and the connection to the application, but the finished artwork visibly redraws internal spaces rather than relying on tracking alone. Give the word a slightly heavier, more settled ink color through outline geometry, while retaining open counters and upright stems. Do not simulate weight with a stroke around existing letters.

The u is the signature letter. Its outer bowl retains a broad conventional curve; its inner bottom becomes a wider, almost level ledge with soft corners and a slightly quicker rise on the right. Both terminals finish at the same lowercase height. This controlled difference between inner and outer contours creates a distinctly held space without making the u look broken, cartoonish, or like the standalone symbol inserted into a word. Preserve enough depth above the ledge that the letter cannot be mistaken for a shallow cup glyph.

Redraw the a's lower counter as a generous space with a similarly calm floor and a slightly tighter right corner. Keep its upper aperture and double-storey construction plainly recognizable. Broaden the M's central negative valley enough to echo that openness, but retain its angular capital structure. The l keeps a short readable foot and its narrower advance. The v remains an unmistakable diagonal letter, with a clean inner vertex and only a small optical correction at the outer point.

Space the word by the apparent areas between letters. Keep Ml cohesive without a collision, prevent excess air around the narrow l, and let the uv and va pairs remain visibly separate. The five letters should feel like one practiced utterance. All distinctive changes live in durable shapes large enough to survive modest reproduction; there are no micro-notches, ligatures, missing pieces, flourishes, or lowered terminals. Deliver one filled, monochrome wordmark on transparent alpha, with no mark or supporting text.
changes: Removed the speaking flick and every projecting terminal.
Made the upper recess shallower, the lower body heavier, and the base flatter.
Replaced the smile-like inner curve with a broad ledge and one softened diagonal rise.
Retained one major asymmetry in the mark while restoring consistent terminal heights in the lettering.
Concentrated wordmark distinctiveness in the u bowl, a counter, and M valley.
revision.remainingTradeoff: The concept intentionally approaches the semantic territory of a vessel. If rendered tests still read primarily as kitchenware, a smile, or a generic U, reject that rendering rather than adding illustrative details to explain it. The descriptions are a study direction; recognizability and originality remain to be assessed on the resulting artwork.

logoPrompt: Create a single standalone app symbol for the Mluva Quiet Vessel concept. Symbol only: absolutely no letters, words, caption, tagline, labels, mockups, grid, frame, or app tile. Use one flat opaque monochrome ink fill, near-black #10131A, on an ACTUAL fully transparent alpha background. The background must contain no white paint, no checkerboard pixels, no colored rectangle, and no shadow. Produce precise, clean vector-like edges suitable for later vector reconstruction. The symbol is one compact connected filled mass, approximately 100 wide by 80 high, with a broad asymmetric recess carved from its top edge. A taller broad left shoulder and a visibly lower narrower right shoulder hold a thick lower body. The right shoulder remains wholly inside the outer hull; no outward projection. Center the open recess slightly right of the symbol's midpoint. Its width is about 42 percent of the whole. Its depth is about 36 units measured from the highest shoulder, leaving a heavy base. The recess connects freely to transparency above. Its left wall descends into one generous inner corner and a broad almost-level ledge; one softened diagonal rises from the ledge toward the right shoulder. Distinct inner geometry, no smile curve. The outer sides are gently convex and unequal, descending through generous bottom corners to a short flattened base about one third of the width. Avoid a semicircular bowl and avoid a rounded-rectangle tile. The overall image should feel full, composed, welcoming, and ready to hold a thought; every characteristic must remain apparent when the mark is reduced to 24 pixels. No strokes or outlines, no uniform-width U band, no enclosed hole, no extra slit, no speech bubble, no speech tail, no microphone, no mouth or eyes, no bowl illustration, no handle, no spout, no flower, no water droplet or arbitrary liquid blob, no gradient, glow, texture, depth, lighting, copied brand motif, or 3D effect. Render only one resolved symbol, generously isolated on transparent alpha, in its final still form.
wordmarkPrompt: Create one standalone custom wordmark reading EXACTLY Mluva: uppercase M followed by lowercase l, u, v, a, with no other characters or words. Wordmark only. Do not include a logo symbol, tagline, descriptor, captions, labels, font sample sheet, mockup, frame, underline, or background tile. Use a flat opaque monochrome near-black ink fill #10131A on an ACTUAL fully transparent alpha background, with clean vector-like edges. No white background and no rendered checkerboard. Start from the upright, legible structure of JetBrains Mono Medium, then make visibly custom filled letterforms with optical letter widths and spacing, substantial medium weight, and clear counters. Keep the capital M recognizable with two straight outer stems and a more open central negative valley. Give lowercase l a narrower advance and a short readable foot. Make u the signature: conventional broad outer bowl, a noticeably wider nearly level INNER floor, soft inner corners, a slightly quicker right-side rise, and BOTH top terminals aligned at the same lowercase height. It must still read instantly as u, with enough vertical depth and no missing pieces. Keep v a crisp conventional diagonal v, clearly distinct from u. Preserve a recognizable double-storey a, enlarge and sculpt its lower counter with a calm nearly level floor and a slightly tighter right corner, and maintain a clear upper aperture. The u and a internal spaces should share the held-space idea without embedding any app symbol in the letters. Keep letters separate and optically space Ml, lu, uv, and va into one cohesive readable name. No ligatures, broken terminals, micro-notches, exaggerated rounded corners, decorative flourishes, accents, stretched letters, stencil cuts, missing stems, strokes, outlines around the letters, gradients, glow, texture, shadows, depth, 3D, or copied brand lettering. Render only the single exact word Mluva, large enough to inspect its crafted negative spaces, with transparent alpha surrounding it.
smallSizeRisks: At a 24-pixel canvas, use a roughly 20 by 16-pixel mark: the upper recess must stay about 8 pixels wide and at least 4 pixels deep, with both shoulders visibly substantial.
If the right shoulder loses a pixel and becomes a pointed spur, widen its terminal inward; do not extend it outside the hull.
If rasterization rounds the recess into a smile, strengthen the internal ledge and shorten the corner transitions in the small optical master.
If the shoulders appear equal, retain at least a 2-pixel height difference at the 24-pixel study size instead of relying on a subtle large-scale offset.
A wordmark is not required to fit inside a 24-pixel app icon. Test lettering separately at a useful reading size and use the symbol alone for tiny launcher and panel surfaces.
The a counter and M valley may darken under small reproduction; enlarge the internal spaces before reducing overall weight.
opticalRules: The mark contains one connected filled body and one exterior-connected upper recess; it has no stroke and no enclosed counter.
Keep overall width-to-height near 5:4. Avoid horizontal stretching that makes the mark a smile or a dish.
Reserve roughly 55 percent of the height below the deepest recess point. The base must look heavier than either shoulder.
Place the recess slightly right of center and keep the left shoulder visibly higher and broader. Use this one dominant asymmetry consistently.
Use a short flat base with broad corner transitions, not a semicircle, full pill, or four-corner rounded rectangle.
Keep all boundary changes broad enough to be read at 24 pixels. Reject decorative kinks that disappear at small sizes.
Center by perceived ink mass and opening balance, not the bounding box alone. Give the symbol clear space of at least one fifth its width.
Use solid full-opacity ink or its light reversal. Theme color belongs to the surrounding product; the shape must not depend on a chosen hue.

In the wordmark, retain exact capitalization and recognizable JetBrains Mono ancestry while redrawing the u bowl, a counter, and M valley. Use optical spacing rather than enforcing equal character cells.
Retain the font provenance and OFL notice if this study later becomes production artwork derived from the bundled JetBrains Mono outlines.
motionRelationship: For a later film study, let the upper recess open by a very small amount and return over the existing 3.4-second breathing cadence, with the heavy lower body and center of mass stable. The change should read as making room for a thought, not filling a container, bouncing, smiling, or reacting to loudness. Keep the right shoulder inside the hull throughout and never detach particles. The existing water imagery can remain environmental; the mark itself receives no ripples, fluid texture, glow, or metaball deformation. Reveal the wordmark once and hold its letter geometry steady, matching the product's preservation of unchanged text. Reduced motion uses the final still mark immediately. This is an optional motion relationship for the study, not a requested app, Figma, film, or brand-asset edit.
